segments.title: Why was Force K sent to Montevideo in 1939?
segments.body: HMS Cumberland was available alongside HMS Achilles and HMS Ajax. Achilles and Ajax had been battered, but Admiral Graf Spee had also suffered damage. Together, the three cruisers probably had enough strength to maintain a heavy blockade off Montevideo. Renown could prevent Graf Spee from fighting its way out. Sending Ark Royal as well suggests that Force K expected to attack the ship if Uruguay could not make it leave Montevideo or it tried to escape toward Argentina. The carrier could strike whether Graf Spee remained in harbour or went to sea. The argument acknowledges that an attack in a neutral harbour would break the law.

evidence.note: Clarke weighs Cumberland, Achilles, and Ajax against the needs of a simple blockade.
Renown would prevent Graf Spee from escaping if it tried to fight its way out.

Force K's deployment is interpreted as preparation for combat if Uruguay cannot compel Graf Spee to leave or the ship tries to escape toward Argentina. Ark Royal could attack in harbour or at sea, with a closing acknowledgement that such action would break the law.

segments.summary: Cumberland, Achilles, and Ajax probably gave the Royal Navy enough strength to contain Admiral Graf Spee off Montevideo. Sending Renown and Ark Royal suggests preparation for a fight.
segments.question: What was Force K rushing to Montevideo to do in 1939?
segments.answerShort: Force K's composition suggests it was preparing to fight Admiral Graf Spee. Renown could stop a breakout, while Ark Royal could attack in harbour or at sea if the ship refused to leave Montevideo or tried to escape to Argentina.

segments.title: Renown's role in stopping a breakout
segments.body: Admiral Graf Spee might try to fight through the cruiser blockade. HMS Renown was intended to stop such a breakout. The German ship had already suffered damage, and a fast battlecruiser would be a much more difficult opponent. This gives Renown a clear purpose among the reinforcements, even if the cruisers were probably sufficient to maintain the blockade.

evidence.note: Clarke says Renown would ensure the raider could not find a way out.

segments.summary: HMS Renown was intended to stop Admiral Graf Spee if it tried to fight its way out of Montevideo.

segments.title: The case for sending Ark Royal and Renown
segments.body: Ark Royal was the closest aircraft carrier, and Force K was the response force. Those were practical reasons to send the formation to Montevideo. Even so, Ark Royal was Britain's premier strike carrier and the newest carrier in service, while Renown was a fast battlecruiser fresh from extensive reconstruction. Large sections of Renown were effectively new, which makes refit seem too mild a description of the work. The combined commitment appears excessive for blockade duty alone, particularly when compared with the Royal Navy's other actions later in 1939.

evidence.note: Ark Royal is the nearest carrier and Force K the response force, but the newest strike carrier and extensively reconstructed Renown constitute a major commitment.
The blockade explanation is questioned against the Royal Navy's other actions later in 1939.

segments.summary: Ark Royal was the closest carrier, and Force K was the response force, but committing Britain's newest carrier and a newly reconstructed battlecruiser still suggests an intention to fight.

segments.title: Ark Royal and a possible attack in neutral waters
segments.body: The force's composition suggests that it was being sent in expectation of a fight. One possibility was that the Uruguayan government would be unable to make Admiral Graf Spee leave Montevideo. Another was that the ship would try to escape toward Argentina. In either case, Ark Royal's aircraft could attack the German ship in harbour or at sea. An attack in a neutral harbour would break the law. The closing joke casts the Royal Navy as more interested in making laws than worrying about breaking them.

evidence.note: Force K's deployment is interpreted as preparation for a fight if Uruguay cannot compel Graf Spee to leave or it tries to escape toward Argentina. Ark Royal could act in harbour or at sea, followed by a joke about the Royal Navy making and breaking laws.

segments.summary: Force K appears to have been sent in expectation of a fight if Uruguay could not make Admiral Graf Spee leave Montevideo or the ship tried to escape toward Argentina.
